# Introduction

Summary statistics help us understand the main characteristics of a dataset.

They include:

- Mean

- Median

- Mode

- Minimum

- Maximum

- Range

- Variance

- Standard deviation

- Quartiles

Example dataset

```{r}

# Create a dataset
students <- data.frame(
  Name = c("Kenny", "Keza", "Robert", "Alice", "Kevine",
           "Anick", "James", "Sarah"),
  Gender = c("Male", "Female", "Male", "Female",
             "Female", "Female", "Male", "Female"),
  Age = c(20, 21, 22, 22, 25, 21, 24, 23),
  Marks = c(80, 75, 68, 90, 70, 88, 60, 95)
)

# Display dataset
print(students)

```

# Using built-in summary() function
The summary() function generates basic descriptive statistics.
```{r}
summary(students)
```


For numerical variables:

```{r}
summary(students$Marks)
```

## Testing statistics

```{r}
# Mean
mean(students$Marks)

# Median
median(students$Marks)

# Minimum
min(students$Marks)

# Maximum
max(students$Marks)

# Range
range(students$Marks)

# Variance
var(students$Marks)

# Standard deviation
sd(students$Marks)

# Quantiles
quantile(students$Marks)

```
# Create statistical functions

can create my functions using the function() keyword. 
Instead of using built-in functions such as mean(), median(), min(), max(), var() and sd().

 We can create one:
 
## Mode Function
 
```{r}
get_mode <- function(dataset) {

  values <- unique(dataset)

  frequencies <- tabulate(match(dataset, values))

  modes <- values[frequencies == max(frequencies)]

  return(modes)
}

```

```{r}
get_mode(students$Marks)
```

## Mean Function

Mean is the sum of all values divided by the number of values.

```{r}
# Create mean function
get_mean <-function(dataset){
  return (sum(dataset) / length(dataset))
}

```

```{r}
# Call the function
get_mean(students$Marks)

```
## Median Function

Median is the middle value when data is arranged in ascending order.

```{r}
# Create median function

get_median <-function(dataset){
  
  dataset <- sort(dataset)
  n <- length(dataset)
  
  if(n %% 2 == 1)
  {
    result <-dataset[ (n+1) / 2 ]
  }else{
    result <- (dataset[n/2] + dataset[n/2+1]) / 2
  }
  return (result)
}
```


```{r}
# Call the function
get_median(students$Marks)
```
## Minimum Function

Minimum returns the smallest value in a dataset.

```{r}
# Create Minimum function

get_min <-function(dataset){
  
   result <- dataset[1]

  for (value in dataset) {
    if (value < result) {
      result <- value
    }
  }

  return(result)
}
```


```{r}
# Call the function
get_min(students$Marks)
```
## Maximum Function

Maximum returns the largest value in a dataset.

```{r}
get_max <- function(dataset) {

  result <- dataset[1]

  for (value in dataset) {
    if (value > result) {
      result <- value
    }
  }

  return(result)
}

```

```{r}

# Call the function
get_max(students$Marks)
```

## Variance function

Variance measures how far values are spread from the mean.
For sample variance, we divide by \(n-1\).

```{r}

get_variance <- function(dataset) {

  n <- length(dataset)

  avg <- get_mean(dataset)

  squared_diff <- (dataset - avg)^2

  result <- sum(squared_diff) / (n - 1)

  return(result)
}

```

```{r}
# Call the function
get_variance(students$Marks)
```

## Standard deviation function

Standard deviation is the square root of variance.

```{r}

get_sd <- function(dataset) {

  variance <- get_variance(dataset)
   
  result <- sqrt(variance)

  return(result)
}

```

```{r}
# Call the function
get_sd(students$Marks)
```

# Combine all functions into one summary statistics function


```{r}

get_summary <- function(dataset) {

   result <- data.frame(
    Mean = get_mean(dataset),
    Median = get_median(dataset),
    Minimum = get_min(dataset),
    Maximum = get_max(dataset),
    Variance = get_variance(dataset),
    Standard_Deviation  = get_sd(dataset)
  )

  return(result)
}

```


```{r}
# Call the function
get_summary(students$Marks)
```
